title: SOFR Daily Rate Observation
summary: SOFR closed at 3.63% on April 29, 2026, down 1 basis point from the prior day's 3.64%. The rate has trended slightly lower over the past week, declining from 3.66% on April 24. This daily observation reflects overnight Treasury collateral repo market financing costs.
key_points: SOFR is calculated as the median of overnight repo transactions collateralized by Treasury securities
why_it_matters: SOFR is the primary short-term lending benchmark. Daily observations provide real-time insight into short-term funding conditions and money market stress.
macro_context: SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate) is published daily by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and reflects the median cost of overnight Treasury repo transactions.
market_structure_context: SOFR replaced LIBOR as the primary reference rate for short-term lending and is used in Fed funds futures, SOFR futures, and as a fallback rate for legacy contracts. It is calculated as the median of overnight repo transactions collateralized by Treasury securities.
